title: (Not oxford) NECROTISING FASCIITIS: The Periocular Emergency
summary: Necrotising fasciitis is a rare, rapidly progressive, and life-threatening infection of the soft tissues and fascia. In the ophthalmic context, periocular involvement requires urgent diagnosis and aggressive surgical intervention to prevent vision loss and systemic mortality.

branches: Periocular involvement is rare but lethal

sections.title: CRITICAL RED FLAGS
content: Pain out of proportion to clinical findings

sections.title: Stages of Clinical Progression
content: Step 1: Early Erythema - Mimics preseptal cellulitis with warmth and swelling.
Step 2: Ischemic Phase - Skin becomes dusky/violaceous due to thrombosed vessels.
Step 3: Bullae Formation - Clear or hemorrhagic fluid blisters appear.
Step 4: Gangrene - Full-thickness skin and fascial necrosis occurs.
Step 5: Systemic Toxicity - Fever, tachycardia, hypotension, and multi-organ failure.

content.explanation: F: Fever & Toxicity; A: Anesthesia of the skin; S: Surface necrosis; T: Tension/Swelling beyond margins.

sections.title: Immediate Management Protocol
content: URGENT Surgical Debridement: Removal of all necrotic tissue until healthy bleeding margins are reached.
Broad-Spectrum IV Antibiotics: High-dose triple therapy (e.g., Penicillin, Clindamycin, and an Aminoglycoside).
Hemodynamic Support: Fluid resuscitation and ICU admission.
Imaging: CT or MRI to detect gas in tissues and depth of spread (do not delay surgery for imaging).
Secondary Reconstruction: Skin grafting or ophthalmic plastic surgery once infection is controlled.

sections.title: Clinical Summary Note
sections.content: Necrotising fasciitis of the eyelids is a devastating condition where time is tissue. Because the eyelid skin is the thinnest in the body, the infection can penetrate the orbital septum rapidly. A high index of suspicion is required when an apparent 'cellulitis' does not respond to standard antibiotics or shows signs of systemic toxicity. Immediate multi-disciplinary involvement including ophthalmology, infectious disease, and intensive care is mandatory.
